title: SSE Event Parser
summary: Parse chunked server-sent events while handling split lines, comments, and multiline data payloads.

testCases.name: parses multiline data split across chunks
ignores comments fields and incomplete final event
testCases.input:
chunks = [
    ": keepalive\nida",
    "ta: ignored\ndata: first\n\n",
    "event: message\ndata: se",
    "cond\n\n",
    "data: incomplete",
]
parse_sse_events(chunks)

testCases.name: parses multiple events from one chunk
recognizes a blank delimiter split across chunks
removes at most one optional data space
handles a long line split across chunks

clarifyingQuestions: Should incomplete trailing events be emitted or buffered for later?
After `data:`, should at most one space after the colon be removed while further spaces stay?
Do we need to parse event names and IDs or only data payloads?
followUps: Return event objects with `event`, `id`, and `data` fields.
Support incremental parsing across multiple calls.
Support bare CR line endings and incremental UTF-8 decoding from byte chunks.
followUpGuide: For event objects, reset data and event type after dispatch, default an empty event type to message, and preserve the last event ID across events. Apply the standard's null-character and retry-field rules; event IDs persist across dispatches while data and event type reset.
For incremental parsing, turn the function into a class with persistent `buffer` and `current_data` fields.

The base solution already handles split CRLF because it waits for LF before stripping CR. To also support bare CR, recognize CR as a terminator and suppress a following LF even across chunks. Decode byte chunks with one persistent UTF-8 decoder so split multibyte characters survive.
complexityAnalysis: - Let N be total input characters and K the number of chunks. The supplied split-and-buffer solution processes characters and fragments once. Time: O(N + K). Space: O(N + K) worst case, including accumulated returned events and partial-line fragment references (even empty chunks cost bookkeeping).
- Joining the whole stream first is also O(N + K) time and O(N + K) space, but makes an additional full-stream copy before parsing.

- An incremental parser that yields each event and discards empty fragments can use O(m + p) auxiliary buffering, where m is current event size and p is partial-line size. A function returning every event must also retain the output.
solutionGuide: Maintain two pieces of state: a partial line buffer and the `data` lines for the current event.
When a blank line arrives, emit the joined data lines if at least one data: field was seen, even if its value is empty. A comment-only block emits nothing. At end of input, discard the partial event.
